name: Izmir
title: Thickness Gauging in Izmir and Aliağa | Ship Hull UTM
description: Thickness gauging in Izmir, Aliağa and Nemrut Bay for tankers, bulk carriers and container ships: hull structure UTM, CAP and pre-docking steel estimates.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Izmir, Aliağa and Nemrut Bay
intro: Izmir's maritime activity divides between the city's container and general cargo port at Alsancak and the industrial coast at Aliağa and Nemrut Bay to the north, where refineries, a petrochemical complex, steel mills and one of the Mediterranean's main ship-recycling areas share the shoreline. Tankers, bulk carriers carrying scrap and container ships all call here, and owners also use the region to decide a ship's future. For thickness gauging in Izmir and Aliağa, the team is mobilised from India and joins the ship at berth or at anchor.

highlights.p: The Tüpraş Izmir refinery and the STAR refinery at Aliağa, with the Petkim petrochemical complex beside them, bring crude, product, chemical and gas tankers whose deck, piping and ballast tanks can be gauged at berth.

Aliağa's electric-arc steel mills import ferrous scrap by sea, so Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers discharging there often carry hold damage from grabs and magnets that is worth gauging before the next cargo.

Owners of ships nearing a fourth or fifth renewal survey weigh steel renewal against sale for recycling. Measured readings taken before that choice show how much steel another five years of trading would require.

port.h: Izmir, Aliağa and Nemrut Bay: three faces of one port region
p: Izmir sits at the head of a long gulf on Turkey's Aegean coast. The Izmir port at Alsancak handles containers and general cargo, and cruise ships call at its passenger terminal, but much of the region's heavier shipping is concentrated on the industrial coast to the north, around Aliağa and Nemrut Bay. There, two refineries — Tüpraş's Izmir refinery and SOCAR's STAR refinery — the Petkim petrochemical complex, a cluster of steel mills and a series of container, bulk and liquid terminals in Nemrut Bay create a steady flow of tankers, gas carriers, bulk carriers and container ships.

Aliağa also hosts the centre of ship recycling in Turkey, a row of yards on the shore where ships at the end of their lives are dismantled. Several of those yards appear on the European List of ship recycling facilities under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, which governs where EU-flagged ships may be recycled, and the steel cut from ships there feeds the same electric-arc mills that import scrap by sea. For our work, recycling matters less as a destination than as an option. An owner deciding whether to put a 20-year-old ship through another renewal survey, or sell it for recycling, needs to know how much steel the survey would demand, and gauging supplies that answer.

Ships stay in the region long enough to gauge because cargo operations at Aliağa are often slow and sequenced: scrap discharge by grab and magnet can take days, tankers may work more than one jetty, and ships wait at anchor in the bay for berths. Izmir has limited heavy ship-repair capacity compared with the Marmara yards, so ships needing a docking typically go to Tuzla, Yalova or yards abroad, and gauging done at Aliağa or Alsancak becomes the pre-docking survey that sets their scope before they sail north.

facilities.h: Gauging locations in Izmir and Aliağa
p: At Aliağa and Nemrut Bay most gauging is done during cargo calls. Refinery and petrochemical jetties allow work on deck, deck piping and certified ballast tanks within terminal permit rules; the scrap and bulk berths allow hold gauging as each hold is emptied, which is exactly the moment to measure grab and magnet damage on tank tops, hopper plating and frames; and the container terminals in Nemrut Bay give access to ballast tanks and scrubber piping during the ship's stay. Anchorage work in the bay is by launch, arranged through the agent. Tanker gauging at Aliağa usually runs in parallel with cargo work, so the plan is agreed with the terminal before the ship berths.

In the city, the Izmir port at Alsancak handles container ships, general cargo ships and cruise calls, where gauging is planned around terminal operations and the ship's sailing time. Gauging is of little use once a ship has been sold for recycling; its value in Aliağa lies with ships that are still trading, or whose owners are still deciding whether they should. For those owners, readings taken on a cargo call can settle the question before a docking slot is booked anywhere.
list: Tüpraş Izmir refinery and STAR refinery jetties at Aliağa — deck, deck piping and ballast tank gauging on crude and product tankers within terminal rules
Petkim and liquid terminals in Nemrut Bay — chemical tankers and gas carriers gauged at berth on deck, piping and ballast spaces
Scrap and bulk berths at Aliağa — hold, hopper, frame and tank top gauging on bulk carriers as each hold is discharged
Nemrut Bay container terminals — ballast tank, deck and scrubber piping checks on container ships during terminal stays
Izmir port at Alsancak — container, general cargo and cruise ships gauged during port stays under ISPS rules
Anchorages off Aliağa and in the Gulf of Izmir — pre-docking and condition gauging on ships waiting for berths, boarded by launch

context.h: Port state control, emissions rules and the recycling framework
p: Turkey's Aegean ports carry out port state control under the Mediterranean MoU; Turkey is also a member of the Black Sea MoU. The Aegean is part of the Mediterranean SOx ECA, in force since 1 May 2025, so ships calling at Izmir and Aliağa burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or use scrubbers, and the wash-water piping on scrubber-fitted tankers and bulk carriers is well worth inspecting while the ship is quiet at berth. Ships trading between Izmir and EU ports carry EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime obligations for those voyages.

The recycling framework also shapes owner decisions. Turkey is a party to the Hong Kong Convention, which entered into force on 26 June 2025, and EU-flagged ships must be recycled at yards on the European List, which includes several in Aliağa. Both regimes require an inventory of hazardous materials and documented preparation, so a ship's final years are planned rather than improvised. Ships approaching their fourth or fifth renewal survey, at about 20 or 25 years, are where the choice between continued trading and recycling becomes real, and a well-planned pre-docking gauging gives the owner the measured steel renewal estimate needed to make that choice on facts.

psc: Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Izmir and Aliağa
jobs.p: Thickness gauging in Izmir is driven by Aliağa's industry more than by the city port. Tankers at the refinery jetties, bulk carriers discharging scrap and container ships in Nemrut Bay each bring a different scope, and owners deciding between another renewal survey and recycling bring a fourth. The common factor is that work is fitted into cargo calls and anchorage waits rather than yard stays.
list: Hold gauging on a Supramax after scrap discharge at Aliağa, measuring tank top, hopper plating and frame webs damaged by grabs and magnets before the ship loads grain.
Pre-docking gauging on a 20-year-old Handysize at anchor off Aliağa, giving the owner a steel renewal estimate to set against a recycling sale before the fourth renewal survey.
Ballast tank and deck gauging on a product tanker at the STAR refinery jetty, in preparation for its CAP survey later in the year.
Scrubber overboard and wash-water piping inspection on a container ship at a Nemrut Bay terminal during a scheduled call, focusing on the overboard sections closest to the shell.
Crack checks by magnetic particle testing on the hopper knuckles and hatch corners of an ageing bulk carrier lying at anchor off Aliağa between scrap cargoes.

logistics: The team flies into Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport, usually via Istanbul, and travels by road to Alsancak or north to Aliağa and Nemrut Bay. Terminal and refinery access, ISPS passes and launches for ships at anchor are arranged through the ship's agent, and we send crew lists, certificates and equipment details ahead so permits are ready on arrival. A Turkish visa is required for each technician coming from India; because scrap and tanker calls at Aliağa are often fixed only a few weeks out, early notice of a likely call lets us have visas in hand when the berth is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can you measure hold damage on a bulk carrier after scrap discharge at Aliağa?
faqs.a: Yes. Once a hold is discharged and swept, we measure the tank top, hopper and side plating, frames and brackets, concentrating on areas with indentation or gouging from grabs and magnets, and record deformation for the superintendent. Suspected cracks at frame ends and hopper knuckles can be checked with magnetic particle testing in the same visit.

faqs.q: Should we gauge before deciding whether to recycle a ship?
faqs.a: If the decision is genuinely open, yes. A pre-docking gauging programme on the structure that drives steel renewal, meaning cargo holds or tanks, ballast tanks, deck and bottom where accessible, gives a measured estimate of what the next renewal survey would demand. Setting that against the ship's earning prospects is the owner's call, but it is then made on facts rather than guesswork.

faqs.q: Can you work at both Aliağa and the city port in one trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Alsancak and Aliağa are linked by road, so a mobilisation can cover a container ship at the city port and a tanker or bulk carrier at Aliağa or Nemrut Bay on consecutive days, with one visa period and agent arrangements for both. Tell us both ships' windows and we will sequence them.

faqs.q: Do you inspect scrubber piping on ships calling at Nemrut Bay?
faqs.a: Yes. On container ships and tankers calling at Nemrut Bay terminals we inspect wash-water supply and discharge piping, the overboard sections and the shell connections, where linings fail and pitting develops fastest. Readings and visual findings are reported with locations so the superintendent can plan repairs before a leak becomes a port state control item.
